item.title: Antare Launches AI-Powered Physical Security and Video Analysis Platform
item.description:
Antare Launches AI-Powered Physical Security and Video Analysis Platform

UK-based company Antare has introduced an AI-based physical security platform designed to automatically process footage from fixed and body-worn cameras. The system converts recorded video into searchable data by transcribing and indexing events as they are recorded.

🔍 Overview

The Antare Console performs real-time analysis of video and audio streams. By utilizing AI agents, the platform can monitor for specific activities, including physical and verbal assaults, medical events, safety risks, and suspicious behavior. Security teams receive alerts and live video feeds through the Antare App.

🧩 How it works

Users can perform free-text searches on recorded footage to locate specific incidents. The platform also identifies patterns across recorded data, such as identifying theft hotspots, repeat offenders, and recurring incidents across different locations.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Encryption Data is encrypted on devices and in transit
Access Control Role-based access for cloud-stored data
Certifications SOC 2 Type I certified; SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in progress

🚀 Availability

  • Current compatibility: Antare’s two body-worn camera models.
  • Upcoming hardware: Antare Cloud Gateway will connect the platform with existing fixed cameras.
  • Future development: Antare plans to launch a proprietary fixed camera range in early 2027.

#Antare #AI #VideoSecurity #PhysicalSecurity #Surveillance

Source: Antare launches AI platform for video security

item.title: Texas freezes spending on controversial Flock surveillance cameras
item.description:
Texas freezes spending on controversial Flock surveillance cameras

Texas Governor Greg Abbott has frozen state spending on Flock AI surveillance cameras.

🔍 Overview

  • A Texas Tribune investigation revealed the state spent over $30 million on Flock cameras.
  • The bulk of that money was raised by adding a $1 fee to insurance policies, supposedly to help fight catalytic converter theft.

⚖️ Controversy

  • Multiple officers have been placed on leave or criminally charged for misusing Flock systems, at least six incidents in Texas alone.
  • The company faces scrutiny for:
    • Data‑sharing practices.
    • Placement of some cameras near playgrounds.
    • Employees’ access to video feeds.
    • Unsecured video feeds.
    • Attempts to avoid transparency.

🏛️ Political response

  • Gina Hinojosa, the Democratic candidate for governor, criticized Abbott for expanding the use of the cameras in the state.
  • Rep. Keith Self posted on Instagram: “From Flock cameras to kill switches, we will NOT surrender our Fourth Amendment rights to the growing surveillance state.”

📉 Current status

  • In recent months, cities around the country have been canceling their contracts with Flock, including many in Texas.
  • The governor’s freeze on state spending comes just ahead of the Texas Tribune investigation’s publication.

#FlockCameras #Texas #Surveillance #AIethics #Privacy

Source: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
